answer: No wick is trusted until the braider has plaited it tight, strand over strand, without a single loose end. Chandler potash ash burner suet seal is the braiding: a seal potash ash burners carry after burning room hearings. The shale is the first plait, braided at dawn; the ripple is the last, braided before the candles are dipped, and the cedar is the braid itself, tight as rope. A cheat must braid 29 false wicks and loose 29 false ends.
